_comment: klt erc supply spec for the sampler_core composed GDS -- the T1
item-11 (power delivery, structural) supply read for this block
(issue #154), mirroring gf180-drone-fc's layout/digital/
erc-supply-spec.json worked example. The ties[] half (well and
substrate tie declarations) is the issue #161 increment, generated
against klayout-tools 0.6.0 -- the first tagged release whose tie
extraction is isolated from the primary connectivity graph
(klayout-tools#2186), so a declared tie can no longer collapse the
routed design into one island with a false erc.supply_short (the
klayout-tools#2169 failure that kept the #154 increment's spec
tie-less).
Run it against the composed, DRC- and LVS-clean cell:
klt erc layout/sampler_core/sampler_core.gds \
layout/sampler_core/erc-supply-spec.json --format json
What this spec asserts, and why each piece is shaped this way:
- Layer/datatype numbers are sky130's own, resolved from the PDK's
`libs.tech/klayout/tech/sky130A.lyp` (open_pdks
c6d73a35f524070e85faff4a6a9eef49553ebc2b, layout/pdk.json's
pin) and cross-checked against klayout-tools' curated sky130
deck layer table (decks/sky130.py: diff.drawing 65/20,
tap.drawing 65/44, poly.drawing 66/20, li1.drawing 67/20,
mcon.drawing 67/44, met1.drawing 68/20, via 68/44,
met2.drawing 69/20). No number here is carried over from
another PDK's spec.
- `stackup` is the fabrication order from the gate layer up
through every routing level this block actually uses.
`klt layers layout/sampler_core/sampler_core.gds` shows the
stream's top metal is met2 (69/20); no met3/met4/met5 shapes
exist, so the stack stops at met2 -- declaring empty levels
would add zero geometry and zero evidence.
- stackup[0] `poly` (66/20, poly.drawing) carries `role: gate`
-- klt erc's own contract requires the gate-poly layer first,
in fabrication order. It also sets `active_layer` to the
diffusion layer `diff.drawing` (65/20), so gate area -- and
hence each antenna-ratio denominator -- is `poly n diff`
instead of raw poly area (klayout-tools #1979/#2001): this
block's ring stages route real poly interconnect between
stages, and raw-poly area would count that interconnect as
gate oxide area it does not have. NOTE: `active_layer` is
honored by klt builds at/after #2001
(cfec44c119b60227ba3593cbb3293029f74e4165); the first tagged
release carrying it is 0.6.0, which is what the committed
erc.json's provenance.klt_version now records -- the #154
increment's documented-exception dev build
(0.5.0+gb15edf5e3a2e) is retired. layout/pdk.json's
ci_klt_install pin (0.5.0) is deliberately unrelated to this
report: it gates the nineteen committed cells' compose-cell
--check reproductions in the PDK nightly, while this report's
committed-verdict gate is ci.yml's signoff-check (a pure JSON
transform over the committed envelope, pinned to 0.6.0 since
issue #160), not a re-run of klt erc.
- stackup[1] `li1` (67/20, li1.drawing) with label_layer 67/5
(li1.label): li1 is this block's local interconnect AND the
layer the leaf cells draw their supply pin text on -- the
67/5 stream carries `vdd`/`vss` pin labels, the per-cell
`*_vdd`/`*_vss` rail labels, the ring-local `vddr` rail
labels, and the array's `nwell_vdd` well-tie pad labels.
- stackup[2] `met1` (68/20, met1.drawing) with label_layer
68/5 (met1.label): met1 carries the block's promoted supply
pin text -- the `vddr1`..`vddr4` per-ring pin labels
(one each, promoted bare pins by ro_array_core's place
stage) plus `vdd`/`vss` rail and strap text
- stackup[3] `met2` (69/20, met2.drawing) with label_layer
69/5 (met2.label): the top level, carrying its own `vdd`/
`vss`/`vddr` rail text. Labels on a stackup level whose
label_layer is not declared are simply invisible to this
read; all three label layers here actually carry supply
text in the stream, so all three are declared.
- `vias[]` bridges the stackup roles with sky130's own cut
layers, per the curated deck table: licon1 (66/44,
licon1.drawing) joins poly-role geometry to li1;
mcon (67/44, mcon.drawing) joins li1 to met1; the
met1-to-met2 cut (68/44, `via.drawing`) joins met1 to
met2. licon1 physically also lands on diff and tap
regions (that is how wells and substrate are contacted);
diffusion/tap are deliberately NOT stackup conductors
here -- the tap side of that path is exactly what the
`ties[]` section below now declares, in its own isolated
second extraction (klayout-tools#2186), so it can no
longer perturb the primary graph this section describes.
- `nets[]`: every supply the block's own netlist declares.
design/sampler_core.spice's `.subckt sampler_core` pins are
`vddr1 vddr2 vddr3 vddr4 vdd vss` -- six supplies, all
declared `kind: supply` so a short between any two reads
as `erc.supply_short` rather than the general
`erc.multiply_driven_net`, and each must resolve to exactly
ONE electrical island (no `erc.unconnected_net` naming it
-- that rule fires on zero matches AND on more than one).
The four `vddrN` names, not the bare `vddr`: the
ring-local text label `vddr` (and the per-stage strap
names `g_vddr_m1`/`s1..s4_vddr_m1`) repeat inside EVERY
ring, so declaring `vddr` as one supply resolves to four
disconnected islands -- one per ring rail -- which is the
netlist's own topology, not a defect: `ro_array_core`
routes each ring's supply as its own rail and promotes
`vddr1`-`vddr4` as four separate block pins
(layout/ro_array_core/README.md: 'the four vddr rails
... stay separate, exactly as intended'), and
layout/sampler_core/lvs.json's `net_correspondence`
carries all four as separate reference-side nets. The
block-level supply names are therefore the per-pin
`vddr1..vddr4`, exactly as the netlist declares them.
- `ties[]` (the #161 increment): one entry per distinct
well/substrate-to-supply tie this block actually draws,
graded by klt erc 0.6.0's isolated second extraction
(klayout-tools#2186). Every entry shares three shapes:
- `tap_layer` 65/44 with `tap_is_dedicated: true`:
sky130's `tap.drawing` is a tap-only tub-contact marker
(the PDK's own layer for exactly this purpose -- the
very layer klayout-tools' erc docs name as the
tap_is_dedicated exemplar), so no `tap_requires`
narrowing is needed and none of these ties is
degenerate (`erc_coverage.skipped[]` stays empty; a
degenerate declaration would render clean_partial and
item 11 would refuse it).
- `connect_to: li1`: every tap is landed on by licon1
cuts and covered by its rail's li1 pad, so wiring the
tap sites up to the li1 role is the real physical
path the check traces.
- `well_layer: null` + `well_boxes`: 0.6.0 resolves a
tie's well region as the WHOLE drawn well layer and
checks every merged polygon of it against that one
entry's single `net` -- and this block's 90 merged
nwell regions tie to five DIFFERENT supplies (70 to
vdd, 5 to each of vddr1..vddr4, measured below), so a
drawn-well entry cannot be scoped per supply. Each
entry instead asserts its group's regions directly:
every well box is the bounding rectangle of one merged
64/20 polygon whose tap reaches that entry's net,
derived from the committed GDS by klayout.db extraction
(not invented), so the assertion is corroborated by
drawn geometry and the box unions are pairwise
disjoint across groups. The cost of this form is
stated in the verdict of record: these ties grade as
`erc_coverage.checked_by_well_assertion` (the weaker
provenance klayout-tools#2255 defines) rather than as
ordinary drawn-well work.
The six entries and how their boxes were derived (all
numbers measured against the committed sampler_core.gds
on klt 0.6.0, klayout 0.30.12, dbu 0.001):
- `nwell_vdd` (net vdd): 70 boxes. The nwell polygons
whose taps reach the vdd island -- the digitizer bank,
the XOR combine tree, and the array's own well-tie pad
labels (`nwell_vdd` sits in vdd's alias set in
lvs.json's correspondence). Union area ~652 um2, about
3.4% of the top-cell extent (bbox
from the whole-die shape klt refuses as a degenerate
well assertion.
- `nwell_vddr1`..`nwell_vddr4` (nets vddr1..vddr4): 5
boxes each, one per ring stage's merged nwell -- the
ring-local rails tie their own wells (issue #161's
'determine from the layout' question, answered: they
do). Each group is one horizontal row at
- `substrate_vss` (net vss): sky130's p-substrate has
no drawn layer, so this is the native-substrate form
`well_layer: null` + `well_boxes` was designed for
(klayout-tools#2273/#2255). The 87 substrate-side tap
polygons (65/44 outside any nwell) all reach the vss
island; the 64 boxes are per-cluster bounding
rectangles of those taps under 2 um proximity
clustering, so each asserted substrate region
independently must hold -- and does hold -- a vss
tap. Union ~704 um2 (~3.6% of extent).
Falsifiability, per klt erc's contract: every merged
asserted polygon must contain tap geometry AND at least
one tap electrically wired to that entry's declared net,
so an untied region (a well whose taps reach a different
rail, a substrate patch with no tap) renders an
`erc.missing_tie` finding naming its bbox. The committed
erc.json is the recorded verdict: zero `erc.missing_tie`,
zero `erc.unconnected_net`, zero `erc.supply_short`,
`erc_status: clean`, all six ties listed in
`erc_coverage.checked` and in
`erc_coverage.checked_by_well_assertion`, nothing in
`erc_coverage.skipped`.
